searchSummary: Rejects the Gospel claim that Pilate customarily released a condemned prisoner at Passover and freed Barabbas instead of Jesus. No Roman evidence supports such a policy, and Pilate's brutality makes releasing a murderous anti-Roman insurgent implausible. The story functions as a distorted Christian memory that transfers guilt from Pilate to Jewish crowds. Barabbas means “son of the father,” and manuscripts calling him Jesus Barabbas sharpen the contrast between the violent prisoner chosen by the crowd and the innocent, self-sacrificing Jesus.

title: A Reflection on Easter.  My Most-Commented Blog Post: #2
author: Diane
description: Reflects on Easter, resurrection, and the centrality of the resurrection for Christianity.
searchSummary: Explains why Ehrman sees belief in Jesus' resurrection, rather than Jesus' own preaching, his death alone, or the empty tomb, as the event that launched Christianity. Jesus proclaimed an imminent earthly kingdom, but followers later claimed visions of him alive and interpreted his death and resurrection as God's saving act. Those claims spread through repeated testimony, transformed a Jewish sect into a world religion, and made Easter the celebration of Christianity's foundational proclamation.

title: Why Are The Gospels Called Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John?
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains how the anonymous Gospels came to be called Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John.
searchSummary: Explains why anonymous Gospels were eventually attributed to Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John. Matthew fit traditions about a Hebrew Gospel and the named tax collector; John was identified with the unnamed Beloved Disciple; Luke was inferred from Acts' first-person travel passages and Paul's gentile companion; and Mark represented Peter's testimony. These assignments connected all four books to apostolic authority, especially Peter and Paul, and distinguished Mark's account from an existing Gospel of Peter regarded as heretical.

title: The Plausibility of the Fourth Gospel: The Chronology of Jesus’s Ministry.  Platinum Guest Post by Dennis Folds
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents a guest argument that John's chronology of Jesus' ministry may be historically plausible.
searchSummary: Argues that John's chronology of Jesus' ministry may be more plausible than Mark's compressed account. John places Jesus' activity across multiple Passovers, repeated Jerusalem visits, and a prolonged conflict with authorities, whereas Mark concentrates the ministry in Galilee and creates a dramatic final week. The guest author suggests that Mark may have invented "Holy Week," the Passover setting of the Last Supper, and related details, while John preserves a more credible sequence leading to Jesus' arrest.

title: A Revelatory Moment about God: Most-Commented Blog Post: #3
author: Diane
description: Reflects on agnosticism, atheism, and whether God can even be imagined coherently.

title: A Full Reply to Mythicist Richard Carrier.  Most-Commented Blog Post: #4
author: Diane
description: Responds at length to Richard Carrier's criticisms and mythicist claims about Jesus.
searchSummary: Responds in detail to Richard Carrier's harsh review of Did Jesus Exist while acknowledging a genuine error about Carrier's academic degree. Ehrman consults specialists and primary sources to defend his treatment of Pilate, Tacitus, Osiris, early evidence for Jesus, Roman records from Palestine, and Earl Doherty's use of scholarship. He argues that Carrier often ignores context or demands monographic detail from a popular book and calls for intellectual charity rather than endless personal attacks over historical disagreements.

title: The Religion of a Sixteen-Year Old.  Most-Commented Blog Post: #5
author: Diane
description: Reflects autobiographically on youthful fundamentalist faith and religious formation.
searchSummary: Revisits Ehrman's reflections on returning to his Kansas hometown and remembering the evangelical faith he adopted as a teenager. He questions why some believers expect religious views formed at sixteen to remain fixed even as adults develop more sophisticated understanding in science, politics, relationships, and every other part of life. While acknowledging intellectually serious theologians, he criticizes otherwise accomplished Christians who resist comparable growth in religious thought and treat his later theological development and agnosticism as simple departures from truth.

title: Richard Carrier: A Fuller Reply to His Criticisms, Beliefs, and Claims about Jesus
author: BDEhrman
description: Responds to Richard Carrier's mythicist arguments about Jesus and ancient evidence.
searchSummary: Answers Richard Carrier's accusations that Did Jesus Exist is incompetent and factually unreliable, while correcting Ehrman's mistaken description of Carrier's doctorate. Through consultation with Roman historians and examination of primary texts, Ehrman defends his claims about Pilate's title, Tacitus's reference to Christ, Osiris's nonbodily afterlife, early sources, Palestinian records, and mythicist use of scholarship. He emphasizes the book's purpose of explaining mainstream historical conclusions to general readers and urges charitable, contextual criticism.

title: Was Paul the Founder of Christianity?  Or Was it Mary, Peter…or Jesus?
author: BDEhrman
description: Asks whether Christianity should be traced primarily to Jesus, Paul, Peter, Mary Magdalene, or others.
searchSummary: Examines whether Christianity was founded by Jesus, Peter, Mary Magdalene, or Paul. Ehrman distinguishes Jesus' proclamation of God's coming kingdom from Paul's message of salvation through Christ's death and resurrection, yet notes that resurrection-believing Christians existed before Paul. He evaluates traditions identifying Peter or Mary as the first witness, competing definitions of when Christianity became distinct from Judaism, and Paul's gentile mission. He ultimately regards Jesus as the founder because every later development depended on his life and followers.

title: Are Paul and Jesus on the Same Page?  Most-Commented Blog Post: #6
author: Diane
description: Compares Paul and Jesus on major issues in early Christianity.
searchSummary: Contrasts Jesus' and Paul's answers to how people receive salvation. Jesus tells the rich man to obey God's commandments, love his neighbor, and surrender his property, whereas Paul makes Christ's death and resurrection, faith, and baptism decisive and denies that keeping the law can put someone right with God. Although continuities exist, their central messages differ: Jesus announces God's coming kingdom for the obedient, while Paul announces the returning Jesus for those saved through belief in his death and resurrection.

title: Could Jews Bury Crucified Victims?  Most-commented Blog Post: #7
author: Diane
description: Examines evidence about whether Jews could bury crucified victims in antiquity.
searchSummary: Reassesses Josephus's statement that Jews buried crucified offenders before sunset. Bart questions whether Josephus means Roman victims, exaggerates Jewish piety and Roman mercy, or describes a universal practice; mass crucifixions during war plainly remained unburied. Even if lesser offenders sometimes received burial in peaceful conditions, Bart argues that Jesus was executed as a rival king and enemy of the state, precisely the kind of victim Rome exposed to deter resistance.

title: Why Did Judas Betray Jesus?  Most-commented Blog Post: #8
author: Diane
description: Explains historical questions about why Judas betrayed Jesus.

title: Reminder!  A Free Webinar on Saturday on “The Bible and Homosexuality”!
author: BDEhrman
description: Reminds readers about a free webinar on the Bible and homosexuality.

title: Burials for the Crucified.  Most-commented Blog Post: #9
author: Diane
description: Reposts a major discussion of decent burials for crucified victims in antiquity.
searchSummary: Reviews four arguments for allowing Jesus a decent burial: Jewish law, Yehohanan's buried remains, Josephus's rescue of crucified associates, and Philo's report of holiday clemency. Bart finds none closely analogous because Romans controlled Jesus's body, Yehohanan's circumstances are unknown, Josephus sought to halt executions, and Philo describes an exceptional imperial birthday concession to relatives. He concludes that prompt burial remains conceivable but historically unusual and improbable.

title: Why Was Jesus Crucified: Bart Ehrman Crucifixion Thoughts
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains why Jesus was crucified and why that question matters for understanding Christian origins.

title: 10 Year Anniversary for The Bart Ehrman Blog!
author: Diane
description: Celebrates the blog's tenth anniversary and its scholarly and charitable work.
searchSummary: Marks the blog's tenth anniversary with thanks from its advisory circle to Bart, members, donors, volunteers, and longtime participants. Over a decade, nearly 3,000 posts brought New Testament and early Christian scholarship to more than 10,000 readers while raising above $1.5 million for charities addressing poverty, hunger, homelessness, health, and other needs. The tribute emphasizes Bart's unpaid writing and reader engagement, recognizes founding members, and restates the blog's paired educational and humanitarian missions.

title: The Blog’s TENTH Year Anniversary!!   Most-commented Blog Post: #10: My View of Revelation!
author: Diane
description: Marks the blog's tenth anniversary by reposting a heavily discussed post on Revelation.
searchSummary: Marks the blog's tenth anniversary by revisiting Ehrman's changed view of Revelation. After decades of teaching it as hope for oppressed believers, close study led him to see a ruthless God who tortures and destroys everyone outside worship of Jesus. He plans to contrast John's vengeance and world domination with Jesus' teaching, arguing that Revelation may corrupt rather than embody the gospel. The challenge is to present this socially and politically consequential critique fairly to readers with strong inherited commitments.

title: Free Webinar!!!  Does the Bible Condemn Homosexuality?
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces a free anniversary webinar on whether the Bible condemns homosexuality.

title: More on Nazareth (Or: Why Non-Archaeologists Should Definitely Not Claim to Be Experts)
author: BDEhrman
description: Responds to claims that Nazareth did not exist in Jesus' time by appealing to archaeological evidence.

title: Did Nazareth Even Exist in the Days of Jesus?  The Weird Claims of Rene Salm
author: BDEhrman
description: Introduces Rene Salm's claim that Nazareth did not exist and explains why that claim matters for mythicism.
searchSummary: Critiques René Salm's archaeological argument that Nazareth was uninhabited during Jesus' lifetime. Later rock-cut tombs do not exclude an earlier poor settlement whose shallow graves would rarely survive, and Salm locates his proposed village site where excavation has not occurred. Archaeologists instead report a contemporary farm, coins from Hellenistic through early Roman periods, and other material evidence. Ehrman argues that Salm lacks archaeological training and rejects expert findings without a sound basis.

title: The Book of Genesis, the White Jesus, and Debating the Resurrection:  Interview with Seth Andrews
author: BDEhrman
description: Shares an interview with Seth Andrews on Genesis, race, Jesus imagery, and resurrection debates.
searchSummary: Shares Ehrman's wide-ranging interview with Seth Andrews, host of The Thinking Atheist. Their discussion moves among Ehrman's interpretation of Genesis, cultural portrayals of a white Jesus, and debates over whether Jesus rose from the dead, along with additional related subjects not itemized in the post. Ehrman regards it as one of his strongest recent interviews because Andrews combines knowledge, intelligence, and skill in directing conversation, and presents the recording rather than summarizing their individual conclusions.

title: Reminder:  You can enter the Blogiversary Lottery!
author: BDEhrman
description: Reminds readers about the blogiversary lottery and its prizes.

title: Gold Members Q&A for April!
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces the April Gold Q&A and invites members to submit questions.

title: Jesus and Sexual Immorality
author: BDEhrman
description: Examines Jesus' sayings on sexual immorality, divorce, and their relevance to debates over sexuality.
searchSummary: Evaluates the claim that Jesus implicitly condemned same-sex relations whenever Matthew uses the Greek term porneia, usually translated sexual immorality. The post argues that Jesus does not explicitly address same-sex acts and that porneia cannot simply be equated with every prohibition in Leviticus 18. Ancient usage could include numerous partners and practices, showing how modern interpreters selectively narrow the term to support present-day concerns.

title: Did Heretics’ Texts Describe Their Incestuous Rituals?
author: BDEhrman
description: Evaluates claims that heretical Christian texts described incestuous rituals and whether those texts existed.

title: How Can Paul Say that Jesus Appeared to The Twelve?
author: BDEhrman
description: Asks why Paul refers to Jesus appearing to the Twelve if Judas was no longer among them.

title: Fabrication, Forgery, and Accusations of (Heretical) Christian Licentious Rituals!
author: BDEhrman
description: Discusses forgery and accusations of licentious ritual practices among early Christian groups.
searchSummary: Examines whether Epiphanius fabricated evidence while attacking the Phibionites, a Christian group he labeled heretical. He condemns their alleged forged books and quotes the Greater Questions of Mary, where Jesus models a scandalous sexual rite supposedly reflected in the sect's worship. Epiphanius claims firsthand knowledge from a youthful encounter and describes elaborate sexual and sacramental practices linked to Gnostic cosmology. Ehrman questions whether either the quoted Gospel or the sensational rituals existed outside Epiphanius's hostile account.

title: Teeth Will Be Provided
author: BDEhrman
description: Recounts a modern scholarly Gospel forgery involving an absurd saying about teeth in the afterlife.

title: Does Paul Know That Judas Iscariot Betrayed Jesus?
author: BDEhrman
description: Examines whether Paul knew a tradition that Judas betrayed Jesus.

title: Christian Pastors Who Have Lost Their Faith
author: BDEhrman
description: Discusses pastors who have lost faith while remaining in ministry.
searchSummary: Explores what happens when pastors lose faith while congregations still depend on their preaching, counseling, rituals, and spiritual leadership. Ehrman recalls his own year as an interim pastor during a period of growing doubt and describes the emotional, relational, and economic barriers to leaving ministry. He profiles the Clergy Project, which confidentially offers community, counseling, career transition, and financial support to nonbelieving religious professionals. The broader appeal is for mutual support across religious and nonreligious commitments.

title: The Apocalypse of John and the Gospel of Jesus: My Final Thoughts
author: BDEhrman
description: Concludes a discussion of whether Revelation's ideology fits the Gospel message of Jesus.
searchSummary: Concludes that Revelation's conquering Christ and ruling saints conflict with Jesus' Gospel teachings on humility, service, love, and care for sinners. John celebrates vengeance, wealth, coercion, and domination while never commanding love for outsiders. Because people model their conduct on the Jesus they imagine, this portrait can legitimize violence and exploitation just as peaceful portraits can encourage justice and generosity. Ehrman asks readers to choose between the attentive, self-giving Jesus of the Gospels and Revelation's wrathful destroyer.

title: The Criterion of Dissimilarity
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains the criterion of dissimilarity as a tool for reconstructing the historical Jesus.
topics: Methods for Studying the Historical Jesus

title: Did Early Christians Believe in Reincarnation?
author: BDEhrman
description: Examines whether some early Christians believed in reincarnation, especially in connection with Origen.

title: Matthew’s Fulfillment Citations
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains Matthew's fulfillment citations and how the Gospel uses Scripture in the birth narrative.
searchSummary: Examines Matthew's distinctive fulfillment citations in the infancy narrative and the interpretive problems they create. Matthew treats some Scriptures as predictions and others as earlier events whose meaning is completed in Jesus, reinforcing a divinely ordered pattern that includes the genealogy and exodus imagery. Isaiah 7:14 originally addresses a pregnant young woman during King Ahaz's crisis rather than a future virgin-born Messiah, but Matthew reads its Greek translation as applying to Jesus and salvation from sin.

title: We Need A Volunteer to Record Audio Versions of the Blog Posts.  Interested?
author: Diane
description: Seeks a volunteer to record audio versions of blog posts.

title: Are the Teachings of Jesus Realistic?  Guest Post by Douglas Wadeson
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents a guest discussion of whether Jesus' demanding teachings are realistic.
searchSummary: A guest writer asks whether Jesus' commands to turn the other cheek, abandon possessions, and love enemies can guide individuals or societies realistically. Their apocalyptic context explains their urgency, while Jesus' use of hyperbole and his emphasis on inner motives suggest principles deeper than literal rules. Because the expected kingdom did not arrive, strict application can fail over time, but thoughtful interpretation of nonretaliation, generosity, and concern for enemies can still improve personal conduct and public life.

title: John of Patmos and the Passion for World Domination
author: BDEhrman
description: Explores Revelation's vision of world rule and domination at the end of time.
searchSummary: Argues that Revelation's final vision is organized around domination and even contradicts itself to preserve subjects for the saints to rule. After all nonbelievers, death, and Hades enter the lake of fire, nations, kings, and sinners inexplicably remain outside New Jerusalem. John's repeated language of almighty power, conquest, iron rule, and kingship establishes a hierarchy: God dominates Christ, Christ conquers earth, his slaves become rulers, and lesser kings surrender their glory. Eternal triumph therefore requires continuing subordination.

title: Reminder:  My Debate on Saturday.  Did the Resurrection of Jesus Really Happen?
author: BDEhrman
description: Reminds readers about a debate on whether Jesus' resurrection happened.

title: O Frabjous Day, Callou Callay
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces the publication of a scholarly book on early Christian journeys to heaven and hell.

title: Revelation and Ancient Views of Dominance
author: BDEhrman
description: Compares Revelation's ideology of dominance with ancient views of power and rule.
searchSummary: Contrasts Jesus' inversion of ancient dominance with Revelation's promise of future rule. Roman society treated military conquest, slavery, patriarchy, patronage, and inequality as natural; Jesus instead made humility, service, sacrifice, and care for the weak ends in themselves rather than temporary paths to power. Christianity's support for people in need challenged Roman social assumptions. Revelation returns to dominance by granting Christ's followers authority after catastrophe, raising the question whether its vengeance and coercion can represent Jesus' message.

title: Wanna join this month’s book club reading?  Check it out!
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces a two-part book club event for blog members.

title: Understanding the Old Testament!  Joshua – 2 Kings as the Deuteronomistic History
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains Joshua through 2 Kings as the Deuteronomistic History within Hebrew Bible scholarship.

title: Why I Am Not A Christian: Is Bart Ehrman a Christian?
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains why Bart no longer identifies as Christian, focusing on disagreement with Jesus' apocalyptic expectation that ultimate meaning lies beyond this world.
searchSummary: Explains why Bart no longer considers himself a Christian even in the limited sense of following Jesus's teachings. Historical evidence portrays Jesus as an apocalypticist who expected God soon to end the present age and establish an earthly kingdom, placing ultimate meaning in a transcendent divine reality. Bart instead believes this material world is the only reality and that meaning arises from what people value, achieve, and love within it, making his worldview fundamentally different from Jesus's.

title: If Revelation is All Symbolic, Why Would the Violence *Matter*?
author: BDEhrman
description: Asks whether Revelation's symbolic language reduces the ethical problem of its violence.
searchSummary: Argues that Revelation's symbolic character does not neutralize its violence. John may not expect every torture literally, but his chosen images reveal a theology of wrath, vengeance, enemies, and domination rather than love, mercy, conversion, or reconciliation. Symbols shape readers' imaginations and can encourage violent behavior; John could have envisioned evil overcome through healing and persuasion but instead celebrates torment and slaughter. The ethical issue is therefore the worldview the story commends, not whether its bloodshed will occur as narrated.

title: A LOTTERY!!  To CELEBRATE the Blog’s 10-Year Blogiversary!
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces a blog-anniversary lottery fundraiser for disaster relief in Ukraine.
searchSummary: Celebrates the blog's tenth anniversary with a lottery whose proceeds fund Ukrainian disaster relief through CARE and Doctors Without Borders. Unlimited $10 tickets provide chances at a private group webinar, a two-person conversation, or a one-on-one session with Bart, with winners helping choose the discussion topic. The post explains the purchase deadline and registration process and frames participation as both an anniversary celebration and a tax-deductible contribution to people facing war-related devastation.

title: Did Nazareth Exist?
author: BDEhrman
description: Evaluates mythicist claims that Nazareth did not exist in Jesus' time.
searchSummary: Argues that archaeological evidence establishes Nazareth as a small, poor Jewish village in Jesus' lifetime. René Salm's reliance on the absence of expensive contemporary rock-cut tombs overlooks the burial practices of poor residents, while excavated farms, pottery, coins, and a hillside house date from the relevant period. Specialists also identify errors in Salm's ceramic, hydrological, and topographical reasoning. Nazareth's obscurity explains its absence from major literary sources and makes it an unlikely invented messianic hometown.

title: Do Textual Critics Have to be Radical Skeptics?  Guest Post by Kurt Jaros
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents Kurt Jaros's guest response to whether textual critics must be radical skeptics.

title: The Most Violent Passage in Revelation, in My View:
author: BDEhrman
description: Identifies and evaluates a particularly violent passage in Revelation.
searchSummary: Examines Revelation's threat against the Christian prophet John labels Jezebel. Her acceptance of eating temple meat may have allowed believers to maintain pagan relationships or evangelize, but John depicts it as sexual immorality and deception. Christ threatens to throw her onto a bed, afflict those associated with her, and kill her children, extending violence beyond pagans and Jews to a church leader and innocent offspring. Ehrman regards this punishment for intracommunity disagreement as the book's most disturbing passage.

title: Two of the Most Violent Passages in Revelation
author: BDEhrman
description: Continues a discussion of violent passages in Revelation and their interpretation.
searchSummary: Highlights two exceptionally violent visions in Revelation. Christ and an angel harvest humanity as grapes, producing a two-hundred-mile river of blood in God's winepress; later, Christ slaughters the Beast's armies and invites scavenger birds to consume their corpses at the Lamb's marriage supper while the Beast and prophet burn forever. These scenes depict vengeance not merely against Rome but all opposing nations. Ehrman then turns toward Christ's threats against dissenting teachers within his own churches.

title: Does Paul Condemn Slavery?  The Surprising Answer–Paul and Philemon
author: BDEhrman
description: Examines Paul's letter to Philemon and whether Paul condemns slavery.

title: What Do You Think?  Is There a Reason to Be Religious If There Is No Afterlife?
author: BDEhrman
description: Asks whether religion has a reason to exist if there is no afterlife.

title: Is the Sacrificed Lamb of God Violent?  More Reflections on Revelation
author: BDEhrman
description: Reflects on whether Revelation's image of the slain Lamb is itself connected with violence.
searchSummary: Rejects claims that Revelation's controlling image is a harmless sacrificed Lamb. Christ first appears as Daniel's cosmic judge with a sword of judgment and later returns bloodied to strike nations and impose iron rule. The Lamb opens the seals that unleash escalating cycles of war, famine, disease, cosmic destruction, and death. These cycles repeat rather than form a chronological timeline, but their source and message remain violent: the former victim becomes a conquering lion who destroys everyone outside God's slaves.

title: Is the Apocalypse of John a Book of Hope?
author: BDEhrman
description: Asks whether Revelation should be understood as a book of hope despite its violent imagery.
searchSummary: Argues that Revelation is dominated by wrath and violence rather than hope, love, or peace. Its central chapters unleash repeated global catastrophes, torment, mass death, and final burning, while martyrs seek vengeance and Christ becomes a conquering lion. Claims that Christians never participate overlook Greek commands telling God's people to repay Babylon with doubled torment. Although Christ first appears as a slaughtered Lamb, he initiates the disasters and returns as king to avenge blood against the earth's inhabitants.

title: When I First Read the Book of Revelation….
author: BDEhrman
description: Reflects on first reading Revelation and later changes in interpretation.
searchSummary: Traces Ehrman's changing interpretations of Revelation from fear and confusion as a teenager, through Hal Lindsey's detailed end-time blueprint, to historical study of ancient apocalypses and a liberal message of hope. Failed predictions and scholarship displaced the futuristic reading, while later close analysis undermined the comforting one. The post introduces his new concern that treating Revelation simply as God's promise to end suffering softens a book whose moral vision and treatment of outsiders require a more critical assessment.

title: Vote on your favorite Platinum Post!
author: BDEhrman
description: Invites Platinum members to vote on recent guest posts.

title: When Did the Bible Get Chapters and Verses?
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains when chapters and verses were added to the Bible.

title: Faith and Inerrancy, In My Case — Did the “Young Ehrman” Get it Wrong?
author: BDEhrman
description: Responds to claims that a younger view of inerrancy caused a mistaken loss of faith.
searchSummary: Clarifies that textual variants did not directly cause Ehrman to reject biblical inspiration or leave Christianity. Their failure to preserve every word destabilized his strict inerrancy, but he continued for years to hold models of inspiration and then a liberal Christian faith despite recognizing errors and contradictions. He ultimately left because pervasive suffering seemed incompatible with an active, loving, powerful God. Claims that he discarded all faith when perfect preservation failed therefore misrepresent the chronology and substance of his journey.

title: The “Young Ehrman’s” Faulty Understanding of Inspiration
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains how earlier views of inspiration and textual criticism shaped later deconversion.
searchSummary: Corrects the claim that Ehrman's fundamentalism included belief in perfect preservation or that manuscript differences immediately destroyed his doctrine of inspiration. He had known about textual variants since adolescence, distinguished inspiration from inerrancy, abandoned strict inerrancy during graduate study, and continued affirming broader inspiration for roughly fifteen years. His eventual loss of faith arose from the problem of suffering, not a simplistic inference from imperfect manuscripts. Ehrman suggests apologetic caricatures can avoid confronting his actual reason for leaving Christianity.

title: Upcoming Debate and Possible Blog Breakfast?  Anyone in San Diego March 24?
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces a San Diego debate and possible blog breakfast.
searchSummary: Announces Ehrman's March 24 debate in San Diego with Catholic apologist Jimmy Akin over whether the New Testament Gospels are historically reliable. The event marks Ehrman's return to live appearances after more than two years and is available both in person and by livestream. The post also invites local blog members to an informal breakfast in Del Mar before the debate. It supplies logistical and contact information rather than presenting either side's historical arguments.

title: Explanations for Why I Left the Faith
author: BDEhrman
description: Responds to biographical explanations offered for why critical study led away from faith.
searchSummary: Corrects biographical explanations claiming Ehrman abandoned Christianity because textual variants destroyed his fundamentalist view of Scripture. Variants contributed to rejecting inerrancy, but he remained a Christian for decades afterward, moving through evangelical and then liberal forms of faith before becoming agnostic around age forty. His timeline shows that fundamentalism occupied only a small part of his Christian life, so apologetic accounts portraying his journey as an all-or-nothing collapse misunderstand both his beliefs and the actual reasons he eventually left Christianity.

title: Gold Q & A:  March 2022!
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces the March 2022 Gold Q&A and invites members to submit questions.

title: Memories of Ukraine.  Guest Post by Douglas Wadeson, MD
author: BDEhrman

title: An Eyewitness Account of Jesus’ Crucifixion!
author: BDEhrman
description: Introduces a modern forgery claiming to be an eyewitness account of Jesus' crucifixion.
searchSummary: Exposes The Crucifixion of Jesus, by an Eye-Witness as a modern fabrication rather than an ancient Essene letter. Its Latin language, knowledge of four named Gospels decades before they existed, inaccurate Essene portrait, and post-Enlightenment removal of miracles reveal anachronism. The account, which claims Jesus survived crucifixion through Essene medicine, was largely condensed from nineteenth-century German historical fiction, demonstrating how an asserted eyewitness identity and discovery story can lend false authority to invented history.

title: Debate Announcement!  Did the Resurrection of Jesus Really Happen?  Two Bible Scholars Debate the Evidence
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces a debate with Mike Licona on whether Jesus' resurrection happened.
searchSummary: Announces an extended debate with Mike Licona over whether Jesus' resurrection can be established historically. The planned seven-hour format allows sustained treatment of ancient miracle concepts, Gospel consistency, eyewitness claims, hallucinations, disciple doubt, the origins of resurrection belief, and whether historical method can evaluate supernatural events. Ehrman and Licona disagree across these questions. The post explains the event's schedule, registration, blog discount, and connection to Ehrman's online courses while previewing the substantive issues the debate will address.

title: Want a Recording of Upcoming Ukraine Lecture:  “Who Killed Jesus?  And Why?” ?
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains how donors can receive a recording of the Ukraine fundraiser lecture.
searchSummary: Clarifies that donors to the Ukraine fundraiser will receive a recording of Bart's lecture “Who Killed Jesus? And Why?” and its question session even if they cannot attend live. The brief announcement supplies links for donating and registering, reiterates that all proceeds go to CARE's work with Ukrainians forced from their country, and notes that Bart will match contributions up to $10,000. It expands participation beyond readers available at the scheduled event time.

title: Our Ukraine Fundraiser:  For those who can’t afford it and for those who can donate for them
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains arrangements for readers who cannot afford the Ukraine fundraiser donation.
searchSummary: Makes the Ukraine fundraising lecture accessible both to readers unable to afford admission and to supporters willing to sponsor their attendance. The event combines Bart's talk and questions about responsibility for Jesus's death, with all proceeds going to CARE and Bart matching donations up to $10,000. Separate registration options permit donated tickets or zero-cost attendance, while every donor receives the recording. Bart emphasizes that the blog should remain open rather than financially exclusive.

title: How Luke Rewrote Matthew’s Nativity Story     Platinum Guest Post by Dennis J. Folds
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents a guest argument that Luke rewrote Matthew's nativity story.
searchSummary: Presents a guest argument for the Farrer hypothesis that Luke used and creatively rewrote Matthew as well as Mark. Luke's nativity transforms Matthew's loosely connected, prophecy-centered account into a coherent story with more sympathetic characters and broader Gentile appeal. The post treats the annunciation, census, journey to Bethlehem, shepherds, and related narrative details as Luke's solutions to gaps or problems in Matthew rather than traditions drawn independently from another source.

title: Young Jesus with the Brahmins in India!
author: BDEhrman

author: BDEhrman

searchSummary: Announces a Ukraine relief fundraiser built around Bart's lecture and question session on who killed Jesus and why. The talk examines Roman responsibility, later blame directed at Jews, source reliability, and whether Jesus intended his death. Admission donations go entirely to CARE's humanitarian work, with Bart matching the total up to $10,000 and encouraging additional generosity. Donors unable to attend live receive a recording, allowing the educational event to support displaced Ukrainians broadly.

author: admin

author: BDEhrman
description: Recounts a humorous modern Gospel forgery associated with Bruce Metzger.

title: Why Date the Gospels after 70 CE?
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains why most New Testament scholars date the canonical Gospels after 70 CE.

title: An Intense Back and Forth on Key Issues
author: FreedomBen
description: Shares a rapid-fire Global Skeptics interview on faith, religion, and critical scholarship.
searchSummary: Introduces a rapid-fire Global Skeptics podcast interview designed around a strict twenty-minute limit. Ehrman and the interviewers deliberately use a compressed question-and-answer format, moving quickly through broad issues and multiple perspectives instead of developing one subject at length. He characterizes the result as one of his best fast-paced interviews because the questions are strong and wide-ranging, but the brief post leaves their exact subjects and his responses to the embedded recording.

title: “In the Beginning” (Part 2)
author: BDEhrman
description: Continues summarizing lectures from a course on myth, legend, and history in Genesis.

title: In the Beginning: Myth, Legend, and History in the Book of Genesis (Part 1)
author: BDEhrman
description: Introduces a course on Genesis as myth, legend, and history in the Pentateuch.
searchSummary: Introduces a course on critical scholarship and the book of Genesis. The first lectures explain why scholars view the Pentateuch as a compilation of later sources rather than a work by Moses, then examine translation problems, contradictions, anachronisms, and historically implausible narratives. Ehrman compares Genesis's two creation accounts, rejects attempts to treat them as modern science, and argues that reading them as ancient myths can reveal their enduring meaning without requiring historical or scientific accuracy.

title: Don’t Forget!  Ask Bart Anything: Sunday!!
author: BDEhrman
description: Reminds readers about an Ask Bart Anything fundraiser for Doctors Without Borders.
searchSummary: Reminds readers about an imminent Ask Bart Anything fundraiser for Doctors Without Borders. Participants can pose questions while their contributions support an organization facing especially urgent needs, and the highest qualifying bidder receives a private one-on-one conversation with Bart after the event. Because the bidding deadline falls that night, the notice directs interested readers to the fuller event announcement for registration, donation, timing, and participation details rather than repeating those instructions.

title: Sting and Thomas.  Guest Post by Evyatar Marienberg
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents Evyatar Marienberg's guest discussion of Sting, Thomas, and New Testament topics.

title: Sting and Pilate.  Guest Post by Evyatar Marienberg
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents Evyatar Marienberg's guest discussion of Sting, Pilate, and the trial of Jesus.

title: Forgery for a Scholarly Audience
author: BDEhrman
description: Compares writing about forgery for scholarly audiences with writing for general readers.
searchSummary: Contrasts treatment of forgery with popular presentation by reproducing the introduction to Forgery and Counterforgery. Early Christian literature contains remarkably few correctly attributed works and many anonymous, falsely ascribed, or forged writings, yet scholarship lacked a comprehensive historical study of the phenomenon. Ehrman's project situates roughly fifty Christian polemical forgeries within Greco-Roman and Jewish literary culture. Beyond establishing false authorship, it investigates why authors assumed authoritative identities, what disputes they addressed, how deception worked, and how ancient critics detected it.

title: Forgery for a General Audience
author: BDEhrman
description: Uses Forged to illustrate how a trade book introduces forgery for general readers.
searchSummary: Introduces forgery for general readers through the Hitler diaries and an ancient literary prank. Konrad Kujau fooled experts with fabricated diaries for profit, while Dionysius forged a Sophoclean play to embarrass Heraclides and embedded acrostics proving the trap. These cases illustrate financial and competitive motives, methods of authentication, and the vulnerability of specialists. Ehrman contrasts them with early Christian forgeries, which were rarely produced for sale or amusement but nevertheless circulated widely under apostolic names for other purposes.

title: Ask Bart Anything!  Blog Event March 6
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces an Ask Bart Anything blog event and fundraiser.
searchSummary: Announces an open-topic Ask Bart Anything event benefiting Doctors Without Borders amid humanitarian crises in Yemen, Afghanistan, and Ukraine. Bart will answer direct questions submitted through live chat, with participation available regardless of donation and every contribution going to the charity. A suggested amount supports the cause, while the largest donor receives a private conversation. The post explains the event format, registration link, timing, and separate bidding procedure for the individual session.

title: How Would We Know If We Found an “Original” Manuscript?
author: BDEhrman
description: Asks how scholars would recognize an original manuscript if one were discovered.
searchSummary: Explains why scholars probably could not prove that a newly discovered early New Testament manuscript was an author's autograph. Paleography supplies broad and disputed date ranges, an author's identifying note could be copied, and agreement with later witnesses would not establish originality. A dramatically different early fragment would provoke competing claims that it preserves an original, an altered copy, or another Gospel, leaving no decisive test even if the object actually were the autograph.

title: Platinum Webinar! March 8.  Why Is the Apocalypse of Peter Not in the New Testament?
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces a Platinum webinar on why the Apocalypse of Peter is not in the New Testament.
searchSummary: Announces a webinar explaining why the Apocalypse of Peter did not enter the New Testament despite its early popularity and strong canonical credentials. The work claimed Peter as its author, circulated widely, was regarded as orthodox and canonical by some church leaders, and offered Christianity's earliest surviving guided tour of heaven and hell. The planned presentation examines why support nevertheless disappeared in the fourth or fifth century and what that reversal reveals about canon formation.

title: What If Damascus Was In Arabia?  Solving a Dilemma in the Life of Paul.  Platinum Guest Post by Gregory Hartzler-Miller
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents a guest proposal about Damascus, Arabia, and the chronology of Paul's conversion.

title: Must Jesus Divide Families?  Guest post by Douglas Wadeson
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents a guest discussion of Jesus' sayings about family division and discipleship.
searchSummary: Examines Jesus' sayings that subordinate biological family to a new community of disciples and even require followers to hate parents, spouses, children, siblings, and life itself. A guest writer connects this severity with Jesus' and Paul's expectation that the present age would soon end, making marriage and household continuity secondary to God's kingdom. As generations passed without the end, later writings attributed to Paul became more family-friendly, showing Christian teaching adapting to a durable social future.

title: Did I Have an Errant View of Inerrancy? (!)  Guest Video Post by Kurt Jaros (#5)
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents Kurt Jaros's video response to claims about Bart Ehrman's former view of inerrancy.
searchSummary: Introduces Kurt Jaros's guest video examining whether Ehrman's youthful understanding of biblical inerrancy, inspiration, and textual preservation contained misconceptions that influenced his later loss of faith. Jaros asks whether slightly different formulations of those doctrines might have sent the young Ehrman along another path. The post presents this as an evangelical apologist's analysis rather than Ehrman's own conclusion, inviting scrutiny of how early theological assumptions may shape later reactions when evidence challenges them.

title: February Gold Q&A: Ask your Questions!
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces the February Gold Q&A and invites members to submit questions.

title: Heaven and Hell at the Scholarly Level (for comparison)
author: BDEhrman
description: Compares scholarly and popular treatments of afterlife traditions in Heaven and Hell research.
searchSummary: Defines the scope and method of Journeys to Heaven and Hell, Ehrman's comparison of Christian afterlife tours with Greek, Roman, and Jewish traditions. Rather than tracing the genre's origins, the book asks how narratives such as the Apocalypses of Peter and Paul, the Acts of Thomas, and Christ's descent shaped theology, ethics, evangelism, and conduct among the living. Ehrman reviews the field's debate over Greek-Orphic versus Jewish sources and redirects attention toward each text's context, meaning, transmission, and practical purpose.

title: Heaven and Hell at the Popular Level
author: BDEhrman
description: Uses Heaven and Hell to illustrate writing about afterlife traditions for a general audience.
searchSummary: Uses the opening of Heaven and Hell to demonstrate how Ehrman presents afterlife scholarship for general readers. The narrative begins with the modern discovery of the Apocalypse of Peter, a second-century work once considered for Scripture and falsely attributed to Jesus' disciple. Its guided tour graphically assigns eternal punishments to sinners and rewards to saints, anticipating Dante. The accessible historical story introduces the book's larger investigation into how authoritative descriptions of heaven and hell arose and persuaded Christians.

title: The Messages of Jesus and Paul:  Basically the Same or Fundamentally Different?
author: BDEhrman
description: Compares Jesus' proclamation of God's kingdom with Paul's preaching about Jesus' death and resurrection.
searchSummary: Compares the substantial continuities and differences between Jesus and Paul without reducing either relationship to a simple verdict. Both remain Jewish apocalyptic preachers who expect imminent divine intervention, value faith, and summarize the law through love; yet Jesus announces a distinct Son of Man and obedience to his interpretation of God's law, whereas Paul identifies Jesus as the returning judge and makes faith in his death and resurrection decisive. Whether these constitute one message remains a matter of interpretation.

title: Jesus and Paul:  Are They on the Same Page?
author: BDEhrman
description: Asks whether Jesus and Paul taught the same message or fundamentally different ones.
searchSummary: Uses the rich man's question about eternal life to expose different understandings of salvation in Jesus and Paul. Jesus answers with obedience to Torah, love of neighbor, and generosity to the poor; Paul would require faith in Jesus' death and resurrection and baptism, insisting law observance cannot justify anyone. Following Jesus is therefore not equivalent to Paul's faith in Christ, leaving Jesus' urgent kingdom message for the obedient distinct from Paul's gospel about salvation through the crucified and risen Jesus.

title: Would Anyone *Invent* the Story of the Women at the Tomb?
author: BDEhrman
description: Evaluates the argument that Christians would not invent women as the first witnesses to the empty tomb.

title: (Re)Thinking Everything.  Guest Post by Glenn Siepert
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents Glenn Siepert's guest reflection on rethinking hell and inherited religious beliefs.
searchSummary: Recounts Glenn Siepert's movement from thoroughly trained evangelical pastor to a more open, questioning faith after his newborn daughter's medical crisis challenged doctrines of original sin and hell. Reconsidering those claims led him to reexamine LGBTQ inclusion, inerrancy, salvation, suffering, and the character of God. His book and What If Project podcast create space for people leaving rigid traditions to explore alternative understandings, express doubt safely, and retain community without being forced back into black-and-white theology.

title: My Response to A Book That Responded To My Book: How Jesus Became God
author: BDEhrman
description: Responds to a book written against How Jesus Became God.
searchSummary: Responds to the evangelical volume How God Became Jesus by asking for a coherent alternative to Ehrman's historical account of developing Christology. His reconstruction begins with a Jesus who did not declare himself God, then traces post-resurrection belief through later Trinitarian doctrine; the response authors mainly challenge individual details without explaining their own sequence. Ehrman concludes that their incarnation claim rests on theology rather than a historical reconstruction that historical methods could establish.

title: The Heart of Jesus’ Message
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains the heart of Jesus' message in relation to the coming Kingdom of God.
searchSummary: Summarizes Jesus' central message as an urgent announcement that the Son of Man would soon judge the world and establish God's earthly kingdom. People prepared by obeying the Torah's true intent: wholehearted love of God and practical love of neighbor expressed through peace, justice, healing, and care for sufferers. Followers could begin embodying the coming reversal now, while anyone living against God's purposes had to repent before the imminent transformation that would reward the oppressed and exclude or punish evil.

title: Preface to My Book on Revelation: Expecting Armageddon
author: BDEhrman
description: Shares the preface to a book manuscript on Revelation and modern expectations of Armageddon.
searchSummary: Presents the proposed argument of Ehrman's Revelation book. He rejects evangelical predictions of modern Armageddon and the liberal claim that the apocalypse chiefly comforts sufferers. John instead emphasizes divine wrath, vengeance, catastrophe, and world domination, saving God's obedient slaves while tormenting nearly everyone else and never mentioning God's love. Ehrman asks whether this celebration of violence and glory can be reconciled with Jesus' teaching on love, nonretaliation, poverty, and service, urging an honest rereading of the text.

title: Still Other Models of Salvation in Paul
author: BDEhrman
description: Surveys additional models Paul used to explain salvation through Christ.

title: Paul’s Models of Salvation: Contradictory or Complementary?
author: BDEhrman
description: Asks whether Paul's different models of salvation are contradictory or complementary.

title: The “Common Era”: Invented to Stop Speculations About the End of the World.  Platinum Guest Post by Daniel Kohanski
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents a guest account of how the Common Era dating system was meant to curb end-times speculation.

title: Paul’s “Participationist” Model of Salvation.
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains Paul's participationist model of salvation as sharing in Christ's death and resurrection.

title: Do We Have Any Reliable Sources for Pontius Pilate?
author: BDEhrman
description: Surveys non-Gospel evidence for Pontius Pilate and its limits.
searchSummary: Uses Pontius Pilate to show why sparse contemporary documentation does not imply that Jesus never existed. No first-century Greek or Roman author discusses Jesus at length, but Roman records for Palestine scarcely survive, and even Pilate left no writings and only minimal archaeological evidence despite governing Judea for a decade. Josephus, Philo, Tacitus, and the Gospels nevertheless establish Pilate's existence. Historical existence must be assessed from available evidence, not from unrealistic expectations about ancient recordkeeping or later importance.

title: Are the Teachings of Jesus Realistic?   Platinum guest post by Douglas Wadeson
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents a guest discussion of whether Jesus' demanding teachings are realistic.
searchSummary: A guest essay evaluates difficult commands such as nonresistance, surrendering possessions, loving enemies, and Jesus' silence about slavery. Their expectation of an imminent kingdom explains why temporary injustice and material security could be disregarded, while hyperbole and Jesus' movement from outward rules to inner motives caution against mechanical literalism. Although these teachings become impractical as a permanent social code, their underlying challenges to materialism, retaliation, and hatred can still guide thoughtful personal and political conduct.

title: How Did Paul Understand Salvation?  The “Judicial” Model
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains Paul's judicial model of salvation and its role in early Christian thought.

title: What Was Paul’s Innovation?
author: BDEhrman
description: Asks what was distinctive about Paul's understanding of salvation and Christian identity.

title: What Do You Think?  What’s It Mean to Study Religion in a Secular University?
author: BDEhrman
description: Invites reflection on what it means to study religion in a secular university.
searchSummary: Asks how studying religion at a secular research university should differ from studying it in a church, synagogue, or other faith setting. First-year students distinguish historical analysis from personal belief, but claims that universities are simply “objective” or uniquely seek truth expose their own caricatures and assumptions. Ehrman leaves the question open, inviting a more precise account of academic inquiry that acknowledges professors' perspectives while explaining how nonconfessional methods examine biblical texts without either affirming or attacking religious commitments.

title: Vote for your favorite Platinum Guest Post!
author: admin
description: Invites Platinum members to vote on recent guest posts.

title: How Important Was Paul, Actually, For Early Christianity?
author: BDEhrman
description: Assesses Paul's importance for the early Christian movement without making Paul the inventor of resurrection belief.
searchSummary: Argues that Paul's prominence in Christianity and the New Testament overstates his influence during his own lifetime. He received core claims about Jesus from earlier believers, faced rival Christian teachers in most of his churches, and sometimes struggled to retain communities he founded. The opponents' writings and most non-Pauline voices were not preserved. Only later did canonical books, Acts, forged Pauline letters, and church fathers elevate Paul as the faith's definitive apostle, often while softening or misunderstanding his distinctive theology.

title: Reminder!  Live Lectures Tomorrow (Sunday 1/30/2022)
author: BDEhrman
description: Reminds readers about live lectures for a Genesis course.
searchSummary: Describes a six-lecture course on how scholars interpret Genesis as history, legend, and myth. The sessions address the Pentateuch's continuing significance, creation and modern science, parallels with older Mesopotamian stories, the historical value of patriarchal narratives, troubling moral behavior in Genesis, and evidence against Mosaic authorship. The course is designed to explain both critical conclusions and the reasoning behind them while showing why nonhistorical biblical narratives can remain intellectually and culturally important.

title: Did Paul Invent Jesus’ Resurrection?
author: BDEhrman
description: Argues that Paul did not invent belief in Jesus' resurrection.

title: An Old Interview on Fresh Air:  How Jesus Became God
author: BDEhrman
description: Shares an older Fresh Air interview about How Jesus Became God.
searchSummary: Introduces a 2014 Fresh Air interview about How Jesus Became God and reflects on the importance of thoughtful media coverage for public scholarship. Ehrman praises Terry Gross for informed questions, careful direction, and allowing authors room to explain their work, qualities that help general audiences engage a book's central argument. The embedded conversation presents his account of how Jesus' followers came to understand him as divine.

title: Major Perspectives of Ancient Jewish (and Jesus’!) Apocalyptic Views
author: BDEhrman
description: Summarizes major features of ancient Jewish apocalyptic thought shared by Jesus and other Jews.
searchSummary: Defines four central features of ancient Jewish apocalypticism: dualism, pessimism, vindication, and imminence. Apocalypticists viewed the present age as controlled by cosmic evil, expected suffering to intensify, and trusted God soon to destroy evil, raise the dead, judge humanity, and establish an eternal kingdom. The earliest Jesus traditions fit this framework by portraying him as announcing imminent divine intervention and calling Israel to repent before the Son of Man arrived.

title: Where Did the Apocalyptic Views of Jesus (and others) Come From?
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains historical roots of Jewish apocalypticism and its relevance for Jesus.
searchSummary: Explains how Jewish apocalypticism emerged when historical suffering undermined the classical prophetic claim that God punished Israel for disobedience. Faithful Jews suffered precisely because they kept the Torah under Antiochus IV, prompting a new explanation: evil supernatural powers temporarily controlled the present age. Apocalyptic thinkers therefore expected God soon to destroy those forces and their governments, vindicate the righteous, and establish his kingdom, the framework later embraced by John the Baptist, Jesus, and early Christians.

title: Reminder!  My Remote Book Event, This Thursday
author: BDEhrman
description: Reminds readers about a remote book event on choosing the next writing project.

title: Are the Gospels Too Early To Have Legends About Jesus?  Platinum Guest Post by Bob Seidensticker
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents a guest argument about whether the Gospels are too early to contain legends about Jesus.
searchSummary: Challenges an apologetic claim that forty years was too little time for legends about Jesus to develop. A guest writer shows that A. N. Sherwin-White cautiously argued myth does not always erase every historical core within two generations, not that legends cannot arise, and offered no method for separating them. Rumors about Jesus already circulated during his lifetime, while rapid miracle traditions around modern religious figures show that eyewitness survival and chronological proximity do not prevent legendary development.

title: The Maccabean Revolt
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains the Maccabean revolt as background for Jewish apocalyptic thought.
searchSummary: Explains how the Maccabean revolt helped transform Jewish history and theology before the time of Jesus. Seleucid Hellenization and Antiochus IV's suppression of Jewish practices provoked Mattathias, Judas Maccabeus, and their followers to fight for religious and political independence, rededicate the Temple, and establish Hasmonean rule. Their non-Zadokite high priesthood generated internal conflict, while the crisis surrounding Antiochus also shaped Daniel and the emergence of Jewish apocalyptic expectations.

title: What Is The Difference Between an Evangelical and a Fundamentalist?
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains differences between evangelical and fundamentalist Christianity.

title: The Prophets of Scripture: A Brief Summary of their Message and Mission
author: BDEhrman
description: Summarizes the mission and message of the Hebrew Bible prophets.

title: The Message of First Isaiah
author: BDEhrman
description: Summarizes the message of First Isaiah in its political and military setting.

title: Special Live Event:  What Book Should I Write Next?
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces a live fundraiser asking readers what book should be written next.
searchSummary: Invites readers to help Bart choose his next general-audience book after finishing his Revelation manuscript. During a live discussion he will present several possible projects, solicit alternatives and reactions, and conduct a nonbinding vote, with a private follow-up available through bidding. The event raises operating funds so the growing blog can continue directing membership fees entirely to charity. Donations are encouraged but financial inability does not exclude participation, and registration proceeds through email confirmation.

title: A Particularly Intriguing Podcast Interview:  Jesus, the Bible, and Early Christianity
author: BDEhrman
description: Shares a Blogging Theology interview on Jesus, the Bible, and early Christianity.
searchSummary: Introduces Ehrman's Blogging Theology interview with Paul Williams, a former Christian who became Muslim and possesses substantial knowledge of the Bible, early Christianity, and relevant scholarship. The conversation addresses Jesus, Scripture, and early Christian history through informed questions that Ehrman believes reach the center of important issues. Rather than outline the positions reached in the exchange, the post recommends the recording as the kind of intellectually serious interview he especially enjoys with a well-prepared questioner.

title: Is the Book of Isaiah the Books of Three “Isaiahs”?
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains why many scholars think Isaiah reflects multiple stages or authors.

title: How Can We Understand the Prophets of the Hebrew Bible?  Isaiah as a Case Study
author: BDEhrman
description: Uses Isaiah to explain how the Hebrew Bible prophets should be understood historically.

title: Did My Shift in Thinking Destroy my Own Views?  Guest Video Post #4 by Kurt Jaros
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents Kurt Jaros's video on whether changes in Bart Ehrman's thinking undermine claims about the original text.
searchSummary: Introduces Kurt Jaros's examination of whether Ehrman's later caution about the term original text overturns his earlier claims about New Testament wording. Jaros, a conservative evangelical who argues that other apologists misrepresent Ehrman, focuses on the distinction between an author's original and the earliest recoverable form of a text. The video asks whether that conceptual shift materially changes how much textual knowledge scholars can claim from surviving manuscripts.

title: Aren’t They Predicting the Future?  More on the Prophets of the Old Testament
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains that Hebrew Bible prophets were not mainly predicting Jesus or the end of the world.

title: Gold Q&A for January!
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces the January Gold Q&A and invites members to submit questions.

title: They Ain’t Who You Think:  Prophets in the Old Testament
author: BDEhrman
description: Introduces the Hebrew Bible prophets and corrects common misunderstandings about their role.

title: The Famous Short Stories about Daniel
author: BDEhrman
description: Concludes a discussion of Hebrew Bible short stories with Daniel and its famous court tales.

title: Jewish Indifference to Jesus and the Problems it Caused: Guest Post by Dan Kohanski
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents a guest argument about Jewish indifference to Jesus and the problems it created for early Christians.

title: A New Course to Watch (Live!) Remotely:  “In the Beginning”
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces a remote Genesis course on history, legend, and myth in the Pentateuch.
searchSummary: Announces a course using Genesis to introduce the historical and literary methods of critical biblical scholarship. Its six lectures examine myth and science, older Near Eastern parallels to creation and flood stories, the patriarchs as history or legend, biblical morality, and the Pentateuch's multiple authors. Ehrman presents the series as an accessible explanation of why scholars reach their conclusions and why readers need not dismiss Genesis simply because its narratives are not scientific or straightforward historical records.

title: Did you know that Gold Members can get the full audio feed in their favorite Podcast Player?
author: FreedomBen
description: Explains how Gold members can receive the full audio feed through a podcast player.

title: How I Begin My Book on Revelation
author: BDEhrman
description: Shares the opening of a book manuscript on Revelation.
searchSummary: Opens Ehrman's Revelation book with Edgar Whisenant's prediction that the rapture would occur during Rosh Hashanah 1988. Whisenant combined unrelated passages, symbolic numbers, Israel's 1948 statehood, and a forty-year generation into eighty-eight supposed proofs, persuading some believers to make life-changing decisions. The failed forecast illustrates how modern fundamentalists treat Scripture as a divine jigsaw puzzle and assume Revelation teaches a rapture system unknown for most of Christian history, despite Jesus' warning that no one knows the time.

title: Did Abraham Actually Do It?  Did He Sacrifice His Son Isaac?  Platinum Guest Post by Douglas Wadeson
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents a guest argument about whether Abraham sacrificed Isaac.

title: My Pet Peeve: Simplistic Answers to Explain Suffering
author: BDEhrman
description: Critiques simplistic explanations for suffering, especially in discussions of theodicy.
searchSummary: Rejects apologetic claims that suffering strengthens victims, improves observers' gratitude, or receives compensation after death. Such answers ignore people destroyed by misery, make others' pain serve the privileged, and fail to explain why a loving God permits present agony, especially when the same theology condemns many sufferers afterward. Ehrman attributes suffering to indifferent natural forces and harmful human choices; if he still believed in God, he would prefer admitting ignorance to defending divine control with simplistic, morally troubling explanations.

title: Bart Behaving Badly: Podcasts on the Problem of Suffering
author: BDEhrman
description: Reflects on debates and podcasts about the problem of suffering.
searchSummary: Explains why confident expertise without knowledge and simplistic theodicies provoke Ehrman's strongest reactions. A Muslim interlocutor argued that hardship enables appreciation of good experiences, which may fit temporary setbacks but cannot explain children dying from starvation, disease, disasters, or unsafe water without any benefit or recovery. Ehrman distinguishes the need for human action from the question of divine permission and considers humble acknowledgment of mystery more honest than claiming extreme suffering strengthens its victims.

title: End of the Year Assessment:  The Blog, 2021
author: BDEhrman
description: Reviews the blog's activity, challenges, and charitable results at the end of 2021.

title: What I’m Reading These Days.  You?
author: BDEhrman
description: Shares recent reading and invites readers to discuss their own reading.
searchSummary: Surveys Ehrman's current reading across literature, ancient languages, archaeology, and philosophy of science. Dickens and Camus illuminate character, faith, suffering, and meaning; slow reading of Homer's Greek makes the Odyssey newly powerful; William Dever challenges claims that archaeology confirms biblical narratives; and Michael Strevens investigates why scientific method emerged so late. Together these works show how serious fiction and interdisciplinary nonfiction support Ehrman's continuing effort to understand human thought, biblical history, and the modern world beyond immediate professional deadlines.

title: On Misreading The Gospels: Platinum Guest Post by Joel Scheller
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents a guest discussion of how readers misread the Gospels and what the Gospels are doing.
searchSummary: Presents Joel Scheller's discussion of John Shelby Spong's claim that the Synoptic Gospels function as symbolic, liturgical interpretations rather than factual biographies. Paul's early letters omit many familiar Gospel episodes, while Spong argues Jewish followers developed Jesus stories within synagogue worship and the annual festival cycle, recasting Israel's Scriptures through midrash. As Christianity became predominantly gentile, readers unfamiliar with that Jewish symbolic setting increasingly treated these narratives as literal history rather than theological liturgy.

title: The Bible’s Best Known Short Story: Jonah
author: BDEhrman
description: Introduces Jonah as one of the Bible's most famous short stories.

title: Gold Q&A (Slight Delay)
author: BDEhrman
description: Apologizes for a slight delay in the December Gold Q&A.

title: Evangelical Support for Misquoting Jesus:  Kurt Jaros, Guest Post #3
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents Kurt Jaros's evangelical support for Misquoting Jesus against some apologetic criticisms.

title: Which King of the Jews Do You Prefer?  Christmas Message, 2021
author: BDEhrman
description: Uses Matthew's birth story to contrast Jesus and Herod as rival kings of the Jews.
searchSummary: Reflects on Matthew's story of Jesus and Herod as a contrast between two kinds of kingship. Herod preserves power through deception, vengeance, and violence against innocents, while Jesus relinquishes power, serves people in need, and ultimately sacrifices his life for others. Whether or not the infancy events are historical, the story confronts modern readers with an enduring moral choice between rulers who exploit others and those who accept personal loss to help them.

title: Two Apocryphal Short Stories
author: BDEhrman
description: Introduces two short stories from the Old Testament Apocrypha.

title: A Better Kind of Fundamentalist!
author: BDEhrman
description: Responds to Louis Markos's critique of Bart Ehrman's former fundamentalism and inerrancy.
searchSummary: Critiques an inerrancy definition claiming that properly interpreted original biblical manuscripts agree with doctrine, morality, and modern science. Ehrman argues that appeals to lost originals and correct interpretation insulate the claim from disproof, while scribes more often removed contradictions than created them. Genesis's creation sequence conflicts with modern science, and Exodus contradicts Genesis about God's name and itself about Egyptian livestock, showing that pre-Enlightenment interpretation cannot eliminate factual problems.

title: Recording of Platinum Webinar:  Six Versions of the Advent of Jesus
author: BDEhrman
description: Shares the recording of a Platinum webinar on six versions of Jesus' advent.

title: If Only I Were the *Right* Kind of Fundamentalist….
author: BDEhrman
description: Reflects on criticism that a better form of fundamentalism would have prevented deconversion.
searchSummary: Challenges a review claiming Ehrman left Christianity because he practiced the wrong kind of fundamentalism and judged Scripture by modern standards. Ehrman notes that he acquired inerrancy at Moody Bible Institute, understands ancient worldviews professionally, and still considers historical, scientific, and ethical knowledge relevant when evaluating biblical claims. Reading texts in their ancient context does not require modern readers to adopt ancient assumptions. He rejects pity based on an uninformed account of his beliefs and reports a fulfilling post-fundamentalist life.

title: Gold Q&A for December!  Ask Away….
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces the December Gold Q&A and invites members to submit questions.

title: Another Fantastic Scriptural Short Story: Esther
author: BDEhrman
description: Introduces Esther as a Hebrew Bible short story with political and literary significance.
searchSummary: Retells Esther as a postexilic Jewish short story rather than a record of actual Persian events. Esther uses her position as queen to expose Haman's genocidal plot, save her people, and secure permission for Jews to defeat their enemies, providing the narrative setting for Purim. Despite never mentioning God, Torah, covenant, Jerusalem, or Jewish observance, the story can be read as portraying hidden providence working through Esther's courage, sexuality, and influence.

title: End of the Year Option?
author: BDEhrman
description: Invites end-of-year donations to support the blog's charities.
searchSummary: Makes a year-end appeal to help the blog reach $325,000 in charitable revenue during 2021. Bart explains that every donation goes directly to supported organizations without overhead deductions and may be designated for one or more beneficiaries. He profiles Urban Ministries of Durham, the regional Food Bank, Durham Literacy Center, CARE, and Doctors Without Borders, connecting their work to homelessness, hunger, education, poverty, emergencies, and medical care before directing readers to the site's donation options.

title: Reminder!  Platinum Webinar on Saturday.  You Platinums Only!
author: BDEhrman
description: Reminds Platinum members about a webinar on versions of Jesus' advent.

title: Terrific or Terrible?  What’s Your View of Christmas?
author: BDEhrman
description: Invites readers to reflect on their own emotional responses to Christmas.
searchSummary: Invites readers to describe whether Christmas brings joy, pain, or both. Ehrman surveys religious celebration, generosity, family traditions, decorations, food, films, and childhood excitement alongside commercialization, unwanted obligations, estrangement, conflict, loneliness, and seasonal depression. Because people within the same family can experience the holiday as either fulfilling or torturous, the post offers no single judgment and instead creates space for candid personal accounts of the emotions, memories, expectations, and stresses attached to the season.

title: Vote for your Favorite Platinum Guest Post!
author: BDEhrman
description: Invites Platinum members to vote on recent guest posts.

title: Strawmanning Ehrman:  Guest Post by Kurt Jaros
author: BDEhrman
description: Presents Kurt Jaros's argument that some apologists misrepresent Bart Ehrman's work.

title: A Suggestive Story in the Book of Ruth
author: BDEhrman
description: Explains the suggestive scene in Ruth and what the story teaches.
searchSummary: Interprets Ruth's nighttime encounter with Boaz and the larger purpose of the book. The Hebrew expression translated as uncovering his feet likely describes a bold sexual advance, after which Boaz arranges to marry Ruth. Her loyalty, initiative, and conversion from Moabite outsider to ancestor of David celebrate family devotion and openness to foreigners, implicitly challenging biblical traditions that excluded Moabites or opposed intermarriage.

title: Do You Want (and Need) a Free Membership to the Blog?  Gift Offer 2021
author: BDEhrman
description: Announces donated one-year blog memberships for readers who cannot afford the membership fee.

title: A Great Short Story in Scripture:  The Book of Ruth
author: BDEhrman
description: Introduces Ruth as a short story in the Hebrew Bible.
searchSummary: Introduces Ruth as a postexilic Hebrew short story about a widowed Moabite woman who follows Naomi to Bethlehem and seeks security through Boaz. Ruth's loyalty, gleaning, sexually suggestive nighttime initiative, and eventual marriage produce an heir in the lineage of King David. By making a foreign woman its resourceful central character, the narrative presents a welcoming alternative to biblical prohibitions against Moabites and opposition to intermarriage.

title: Why Doesn’t Paul Say More about the Historical Jesus?  Other Options.
author: BDEhrman
description: Explores further explanations for why Paul says little about the historical Jesus.

title: But Why Doesn’t Paul Say More About the Historical Jesus?
author: BDEhrman
description: Asks why Paul does not say more about Jesus' earthly life and teachings.

title: An Evangelical Apologist Who *Supports* My Book Misquoting Jesus!
author: BDEhrman

title: My New Great Courses Offering, Just Out!
author: BDEhrman
